expectations.text: States plainly that the not-empty check is insufficient
expectations.evidence: "the test you added targets none of them" and "A non-empty check would have been green all three weeks"

expectations.text: Identifies the COALESCE to zero as the mechanism that made the failure silent
expectations.evidence: "a join on a renamed column produced nulls, and COALESCE(x, 0) turned those nulls into plausible zeros" and "COALESCE(NULL, 0) is except: pass for data"

expectations.text: Recommends reconciliation against a source of truth, not only shape checks
expectations.evidence: Table includes "Reconciliation — SUM(revenue) in the warehouse vs. the billing system / ledger, tolerance-bounded, daily"

expectations.text: Recommends that assertions run before publication rather than after, so bad data cannot reach the dashboard
expectations.evidence: "they block publication: build to staging, assert, promote only on pass. A check that emails after the dashboard updates is the problem restated."

expectations.text: Recommends a data contract or schema check so an upstream rename fails loudly and attributably
expectations.evidence: "Data contract on ingest — explicit column list / schema assertion on the upstream source, pipeline halts on mismatch"

expectations.text: Recommends volume or null-rate assertions rather than only a non-empty check
expectations.evidence: "Drop the coalesce; assert null rate on the join key" and "Volume with a floor and same-weekday baseline"

expectations.text: Treats three weeks of nobody noticing as a detection gap worth its own fix
expectations.evidence: Entire framing around "a check that cannot fail" and "Class sweep — the step that usually gets skipped" treats detection as a systemic gap

expectations.text: Explains why a silently wrong number is more dangerous than a failed pipeline
expectations.evidence: Shows why silent failure is bad (looks plausible, can't distinguish wrong from right) but does not explicitly explain why it is more dangerous than a failed pipeline
